clue.text: Aid to driver's prospect, we'll engage one cracking whips

indicators.note: to engage something here is to hold it within, so the pronoun's letters enclose the rest

parts.note: we'll stands for we will, and only the pronoun we supplies letters
one is A, the indefinite article

indicators.note: cracking means breaking apart, so the letters of whips are rearranged

explanation.surface: A motorist's view gets help from someone who promises to take on a whip-cracker.
explanation.walkthrough: The whips are not cracked by anyone: 'cracking' tells you to break up their letters, and 'engage' sets them, after A, inside the pronoun. A wash-wipe is a car's windscreen washer-and-wiper system.
explanation.definitionFit: The wash-wipe clears the windscreen, so it helps the motorist see the road ahead.

clue.text: Doings at Davos? Tense porter's employed with gains around (12, two words)

indicators.note: around means the word for gains wraps about the jumbled letters
employed suggests letters being put to work in a new arrangement

parts.note: first part of WINS, gains, which is split to hold the rest
T for tense plus the letters of porter's, rearranged
last letter of WINS closes the shell

explanation.surface: A tense hotel porter is hired on good pay at a Swiss resort.
explanation.walkthrough: T (tense, grammar abbreviation) joins PORTERS in the anagram, all inside WINS. Davos is a Swiss ski resort, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Skiing, bobsleigh and similar activities are what visitors to the Alpine resort do, an example-style definition.

clue.text: Dog, one breed that's trained with measure of dash

parts.note: one is A, the indefinite article

indicators.note: trained means taught to behave differently, so the letters of breed are rearranged

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure, and an en dash is a dash of that width

explanation.surface: A dog of a certain breed is schooled with a hint of verve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breed' looks like part of the dog-show surface, but it is the fodder that 'trained' rearranges. An en dash is the printer's dash one en wide.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aberdeen is a Scottish terrier, a breed of dog named after the city.

clue.text: Instrument for chopping a slate suitable for one's rockery

parts.note: a sax is a slater's hammer for cutting roofing slates
taken as written
a slate is a kind of roofing tile

explanation.surface: A tool for cutting slate is recommended for building a garden rockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' suggests music and the saxophone, but here SAX is the slater's chopper.
explanation.definitionFit: Saxatile describes plants and creatures living among rocks, which suits the stony setting of a rock garden.

clue.text: Last of a casserole used as starter — to avoid this?

indicators.note: 'Last of' points to the final letter of the stew phrase, which is the one moved
used as starter says that letter goes to the front, as a starter begins a meal

parts.note: a stew is a casserole, a dish slowly cooked in liquid

explanation.surface: Serving the remains of a casserole as the next meal's first course saves throwing food away.
explanation.walkthrough: In A STEW, 'Last of' picks the closing W and 'used as starter' moves it to the front. The question mark marks the definition as an inference from the frugal cook's motive.
explanation.definitionFit: Serving leftovers is a way of avoiding throwing good food away, the squandering the answer names.

clue.text: Producer of ferrous sulphate modified skin shade

indicators.note: modified means changed, so the letters of skin are put in another order

parts.note: the letters of skin, rearranged
a shade or tint of colour

explanation.surface: A chemical compound causes a change in skin colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Inkstone is a mineral containing iron sulphate, once used in making ink, so it is a source of the salt.

clue.text: Saint Simon? (Could be a catch)

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the forename of the singer-songwriter ... Simon
third meaning: a variant spelling of pawl, a pivoted catch that engages a ratchet's teeth

explanation.surface: A query whether a man called Simon was a saint, with an aside that he might be a good match.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate senses: the apostle, the American singer's first name, and an old spelling of pawl, the ratchet catch; 'Could be' signals that this spelling is a less usual one.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle is known as St Paul, the singer is Paul Simon, and Chambers lists the word as a variant of pawl, a ratchet catch.

clue.text: To go through exercises run quickly round area

indicators.note: round means the word for quickly goes about the area letter

parts.note: physical education
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
vite is a musical direction meaning quickly
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Gym exercises: running fast in circles around a space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run quickly' reads as one phrase but splits into R and VITE, which goes round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Perviate is a rare verb meaning to pass through or penetrate a way, from Latin pervius.

clue.text: Some real barren mounts, bleak in the Cairngorms?

indicators.note: in a down entry, mounting means climbing upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top
some means only a portion of the following words is taken

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A description of the bare, bleak Scottish mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cairngorms are Scottish mountains, flagging a Scots word: blae means bleak or livid blue-grey.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect the word means livid or bleak and sunless, so it suits the Highland setting.

clue.text: Wretched waste in the sea

definitions.meaning: first meaning: miserable, low in spirits
second meaning: to squander money, an old slang verb

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a gloomy picture of rubbish dumped at sea, but it is three separate senses of one colour word.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour word also means depressed, can be a verb meaning squander, and 'the blue' is poetic for the ocean.

clue.text: Old dance? Assume a spree is wrong for it

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the letters must be arranged afresh

parts.note: all twelve letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: Going on a binge would be the wrong approach to a stately old dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The passemeasure was a stately Italian dance of the 16th century, related to the passamezzo.

clue.text: What's smoked oyster I've trimmed, included in Spanish dish?

indicators.note: included in says the trimmed shellfish sits within the rice dish

parts.note: paella is the Spanish rice dish from Valencia

indicators.note: trimmed means cut back, so the shellfish word loses the letters of I've

parts.note: a native is an oyster raised in British waters, especially a Whitstable or Colchester oyster
taken as the letters of I've, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Is a smoked oyster, shorn of my additions, what goes into the paella?
explanation.walkthrough: 'included in' sets the trimmed oyster after the first two letters of the rice dish. Native is the British name for a home-grown oyster, a sense non-British solvers rarely meet.
explanation.definitionFit: A panatella is a long thin cigar, something a person smokes.

clue.text: Bond girlfriend no longer enthralled by union

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the National Union of Students
a former partner

explanation.surface: A James Bond story: a former Bond girl captivated by a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' with its capital suggests 007, but it simply means a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A nexus is a connection or link, the same sense as a bond tying things together.

clue.text: Malay craft fixed oars up, not old

indicators.note: fixed as in rigged or rearranged, so the letters are shuffled into new order
not old tells us to drop the letter standing for old

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Malaysian boats have their oars secured and raised.
explanation.walkthrough: O is the abbreviation for old: remove it from OARS UP and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Praus (or proas) are fast Malay sailing boats, so the plural fits craft.

clue.text: Feature of nude, informal? Artist added in touches

indicators.note: added in means put inside, so the artist goes within the other word

parts.note: a slang word for breasts, a feature of a nude
Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A painter adds finishing touches to an informal nude study.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait can mean a stroke or touch, as of a pen or brush, so the plural matches touches.

clue.text: Eastern vessel in trouble, second going for quays

indicators.note: in trouble means disturbed or upset, so the letters are disordered
going means departing, so the abbreviation for second leaves

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: An Eastern ship is in difficulty and a second is heading for the quays.
explanation.walkthrough: E plus VESSEL loses one S, and the six letters left are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A levee is an embankment or landing place on a river, so quays are a fair synonym.

clue.text: Expectant woman's affliction? Reduced energy immobilizes end of pregnancy

indicators.note: reduced means cut down to its abbreviation, a single letter

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy
clamps holds fast, as a wheel clamp immobilizes a car

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of the following word

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: A worrying complication: low energy that leaves a woman unable to move late in pregnancy.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclampsy, or eclampsia, is a dangerous convulsive condition that can strike a woman during pregnancy.

clue.text: Chinese communist exchanging extremes for religion

indicators.note: the extremes are the first and last letters, which swap places

parts.note: a Maoist follows the communism of Mao Zedong

explanation.surface: A follower of Mao trades in radical positions for a faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanging extremes' swaps the M and T at the two ends of MAOIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Taoism is the Chinese philosophy and faith rooted in the teachings of Laozi.

clue.text: Signifying 'doer', one brought in untangled a tangle

indicators.note: brought in means taken inside, so the letter for one joins the group
untangled means sorted out, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is called in to sort out a mess, as a doer would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Untangled a tangle' looks circular, but tangle is just the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar an agential suffix such as -er marks the agent, the one who performs the action.

clue.text: Silence one noisy row? Increasingly tricky

parts.note: the hushing sound
the Roman numeral
F is forte, loud in music
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: Someone tries to quieten a loud argument, and things get trickier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noisy row' reads as a quarrel, but it splits into F (forte) and TIER, a row of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Shifty means evasive or deceitful, so the comparative means more so.

clue.text: Noblewoman is bent, in grip of chronic fatigue

indicators.note: in the grip of means held tightly inside the other word

parts.note: first letter of ME, myalgic encephalomyelitis
arches means curves or bends

explanation.surface: An aristocratic lady is stooped, suffering from long-term exhaustion.
explanation.walkthrough: ME is myalgic encephalomyelitis, known as chronic fatigue syndrome.
explanation.definitionFit: A marchese is an Italian marquise, the wife of a marchese or a lady of that rank.

clue.text: Spain in grip of opulent foreign empire

indicators.note: in the grip of means held inside, so the country letter sits within

parts.note: first letter of RICH, opulent
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Spain is held by a wealthy foreign power.
explanation.definitionFit: Reich is the German word for empire or realm, as in the Third Reich.

clue.text: Cheer in school for what Scottish climber attempts?

indicators.note: in places the cheer inside the word for school

parts.note: first letter of GAM, a school of whales
a shout of encouragement

explanation.surface: Pupils give a rousing cheer for a mountaineer from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: A gam is a school of whales. A Graham is a Scottish hill between 2,000 and 2,500 feet, a list hillwalkers set out to climb.
explanation.definitionFit: Grahams, like Munros, are classified Scottish summits that walkers aim to bag.

clue.text: Woven lisle, new purchase by retailer

indicators.note: woven means interlaced, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A shop stocks up on new woven lisle stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Sell-in is the trade term for goods bought by retailers from the manufacturer, as opposed to sell-through to customers.

clue.text: Lost movement in Holst I restored

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the following words

parts.note: the letters straddling the three words

explanation.surface: A missing movement of a Holst work has been reinstated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost movement' suggests a missing part of a symphony like The Planets; 'Lost' really marks an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stire is an obsolete form of stir, so a movement in a word no longer used.

clue.text: Sliver of noisette consumed red?

indicators.note: a sliver is a tiny piece, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter
consumed as food

explanation.surface: A small piece of noisette was eaten, perhaps raw in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' is not the colour: red (or redd) is a dialect verb meaning to tidy up, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Redd or red means to put in order or clear up, the same as tidying something.

clue.text: Fabric mark? A firm's upset with this

definitions.text: Fabric mark? A firm's upset with this

indicators.note: upset means overturned and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: these letters plus the answer make up the anagram

explanation.surface: A company is annoyed about a flaw in its cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: 'upset' scrambles FABRIC MARK, whose letters are those of A FIRM together with the answer ('this'), so take A FIRM away and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: In Chambers a brack is a flaw or defect in woven cloth, the kind of blemish a fabric firm would rue.

clue.text: Early Irish settlers having forewarning about e.g. Columba

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the warning word wraps around the saint

parts.note: first letter of OMEN
Columba was a saint, abbreviated ST

explanation.surface: Early settlers in Ireland had warning of St Columba's arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ostmen were the Norse or Danish settlers in Ireland, literally 'east men'.

clue.text: Dip in the loch section, low but rising?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for section

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: to low is to moo like cattle

explanation.surface: A walker asks whether a low part of a Scottish lake is getting deeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' is the verb, a cow's sound. 'In the loch' marks a Scots word: soom is Scots for swim.
explanation.definitionFit: Soom is the Scots form of swim, and a dip is a brief swim.

clue.text: Child holding adult perfectly (4, three words)

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the small child word grips the adult letter

parts.note: first part of TOT, a small child
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A small child is held perfectly by a grown-up.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'to a T' means exactly or precisely right.

clue.text: Edible seaweed? Me neither!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Japanese seaweed used to wrap sushi
second meaning: the reply '...' split into two words

explanation.walkthrough: The two halves read as a dialogue: someone offers seaweed and the reply is a refusal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nori is dried laver eaten in Japanese cooking, and the reply 'nor I' agrees with someone else's refusal.

clue.text: Abbreviated transactions shut out the known facts

parts.note: tr. is an abbreviation for transactions
the letters of shut, rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Truths are established facts, things known to be so.

clue.text: Mackellar's unable to sing properly, poorly about opening of opera

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for poorly wraps the letter

rest of ROPY

explanation.definitionFit: Roopy is Scots for hoarse, and a hoarse voice cannot sing in tune.

clue.text: A day I had in France, so long there

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for day
taken as written

explanation.surface: A day spent in France seemed to last a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There' points back to France: the farewell is French.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is French for goodbye, which in English is 'so long'.

clue.text: Feature of breakfast course round oven (9, two words)

an oast is a kiln for drying hops
